topic: Group 2 (industry/startup) plan: three product wedges, Delphi-certificate edge, 30/60/90-day proof of concept, open funding calls, regulatory path
summary:
Partial result from a 7-minute run. Funding dates were opened today (2026-11-13) and are sourced; the wedges, the 30/60/90 plan and most of the regulatory path are my proposal built on the two briefs and the two earlier agent files, and the fire-standard texts could not be opened (403).

THREE WEDGES
W1. Fire-test triage for bio-based ("green") fire-retardant coatings. First customer: university or design-school materials labs and small coating makers who cannot get test slots (the pain point in the 13 Nov brief). Delphi adds an elimination certificate: a machine-checked statement of which candidates a named test would reject, with the data and assumptions attached, so scarce slots go to survivors. A competitor's simulation or screening score has no checkable proof and no public record. Regulatory path: reaction-to-fire classification of interior finishes (US ASTM E84 classes under the building code; EU EN 13501-1 Euroclasses), done by an accredited lab. The certificate is pre-screening only and never replaces the test. Standard texts not opened in this run.
W2. Law-constrained printed panel, proof of concept on Formlabs. First customer: an architecture practice's fabrication arm; the earlier file shows Fab.Pub has a public material-intake route and a GBP 250 minimum budget. Delphi adds a per-part certificate that the geometry obeys the stated morphology laws within stated bounds, plus a nanopublication record. Regulatory path: for a temporary installation, structural engineer sign-off (the earlier file shows load tests by an independent engineer on a prior piece) plus the venue's fire requirement, which leads back to W1. Permanent building use would need full product certification, out of scope for 90 days.
W3. Zebot and locomotion design certificates. First customer: biobot and soft-robotics research labs, then funders. Delphi adds a pre-registered, frozen prediction (for example a fin or body constraint in a passive glide surrogate) checked against a printed model. Regulatory path: a research tool is not a medical device unless its intended use makes it one (FDA page opened). Any live zebrafish or zebrafish-cell work needs institutional animal-care approval and biosafety review (not opened); a purely mechanical zebrafish-inspired robot needs neither.

30/60/90 (proposal, unsourced)
Day 30: W1, write the pass/fail rule of one fire test as a formal statement, collect published small-scale burn data for 10-20 bio-based coatings, freeze the predictions. W2, pick one Formlabs resin and one law, print coupons. W3, freeze one glide-surrogate prediction.
Day 60: W1, bench-scale burn test on 3-5 candidates at a partner lab (cone calorimeter or small-flame). W2, print one panel and measure it against the certificate. W3, print and drop-test the surrogate.
Day 90: W1, one accredited test on the best survivor, publish the hit/miss table including failures. W2, hand the panel, certificate and report to the practice with a priced pilot offer. W3, short report and funding submission.

FUNDING, opened 13 Nov 2026
- EPSRC Materials Innovation Programme Digital Materials Sandpit: closes 26 Nov 2026 16:00 UK, total GBP 7,125,000, UK research organisations only; industry can partner unfunded. This is the only near-term materials call and needs a UK academic lead.
- EIC Accelerator: short proposals any time; full-proposal batch dates 20 Jan, 17 Mar, 1 Sep and 4 Nov 2027.
- EIC Pathfinder Open: stage 1 on 25 Feb 2027, stage 2 on 16 Sep 2027; Challenges 29 Sep 2027; grants up to EUR 4 million.
- ARPA-H: four Mission Office ISOs accepted on a rolling basis; the page says there are no open small business opportunities. Fit is weak unless W3 is framed as health.
- NSF SBIR/STTR: current solicitations NSF 26-510 and 26-511; the only date on the page (4 Nov 2026) has passed and applies to transition cases. Whether Project Pitch is open was not confirmed.
- sbir.gov home page listed no open topics; the topic search was not opened. Innovate UK: only one Innovate UK-funded call appeared on page 1 of 4 (critical minerals, closes 7 Jan 2027, not a fit).

lay_summary: The group wants to sell three things: a way to guess which plant-based fire coatings will fail a burn test before paying for the test, a 3D-printed building panel that follows nature's shape rules, and designs for small fish-inspired robots.
What makes them different is a certificate: a computer-checked proof, like a maths teacher marking every step, that anyone can re-check.
In three months the plan is to make predictions and lock them, then test a few samples in a lab, then show the results, including the misses.
We looked for grant money today and found one UK materials call closing on 26 November 2026 and European calls with dates in early 2027; we could not confirm an open US small-business call.
Real fire safety still needs the official lab test; the certificate only helps choose what to send.

glossary.wedge: A small first product that gets a company its first customer.
glossary.certificate (Delphi): A computer-checked proof that a design or prediction follows a stated rule, with the data attached.
glossary.elimination certificate: A proof that a candidate would fail a test, so it need not be tested.
glossary.Lean: A computer language for writing proofs that a machine checks.
glossary.nanopublication: A tiny, citable public record of one claim and its source.
glossary.proof of concept: A small build showing an idea can work.
glossary.fire-retardant coating: A layer painted on a material to slow burning.
glossary.reaction-to-fire classification: A grade for how easily a material burns and spreads flame.
glossary.ASTM E84: A US tunnel test for flame spread and smoke of surface materials (text not opened here).
glossary.EN 13501-1 / Euroclass: The European fire grading system for building products (text not opened here).
glossary.cone calorimeter: A bench instrument that measures heat released by a small burning sample.
glossary.accredited lab: A test lab officially approved to issue results regulators accept.
glossary.zebot: The group's word for a zebrafish-inspired or zebrafish-cell robot.
glossary.biobot: A tiny machine made from living cells.
glossary.passive glide surrogate: An unpowered model dropped or launched to measure how a shape glides.
glossary.SBIR/STTR: US grant programmes for small technology firms.
glossary.Project Pitch: A short first-step summary NSF asks for before a full proposal.
glossary.ARPA-H: A US agency funding high-risk health research.
glossary.ISO (ARPA-H): An always-open call for new ideas in an office's area.
glossary.EIC Accelerator / Pathfinder: European Innovation Council funding for start-ups and for early research.
glossary.EPSRC / UKRI / Innovate UK: UK public research and innovation funders.
glossary.sandpit: A funder-run workshop where teams form and pitch projects.
glossary.medical device: A product legally defined by its intended health use.
glossary.pre-registered / frozen prediction: A prediction written down and locked before the test.
glossary.resin: The liquid a Formlabs printer hardens into a solid part.
